_comment: System tests and bug reports (FACTORY.md §4b, §4c). Copy to .github/factory-testing.json to turn them on for this repo. With system_tests true, the Test Planner runs between the Planner and the Architect, writes system-tests/test-plan.md and system-tests/test-data.md into the epic's change folder, and opens one test(<epic>) sub-issue per case; the Dispatcher releases each case to factory:manual-test once the code it depends on is assembled, and a human comments exactly 'Test Passed' or 'Test Failed' on it. An absent or unparseable file means system_tests false: no Test Planner, no test sub-issues, and every other behaviour exactly as before. mode 'gate' (the default when the file is present) holds an epic short of factory:epic-ready until every open case has passed and no bug is open; 'advisory' flips the epic as it does today and lists the open cases and bugs as unverified. mode has no effect on a repo with no epic branch (epics false): there the code first reaches a shared branch at gate GS, so the cases run on staging and their verdicts are evidence in the promotion PR, never a hold — gate G3 is a human's merge click. run_on says where a human runs the cases: 'epic' (the default when absent) releases each case as the tasks it depends on are assembled onto the epic branch, to be run on the epic's preview environment; 'staging' lets the epic reach factory:epic-ready on assembly alone, gate GS puts it on staging, and the Dispatcher releases each case once the tasks it depends on are factory:in-staging — cases and bugs then never hold GS, their verdicts are evidence at G3, and mode has no effect (the same posture as epics false). A staging approver (falling back to the release list) can comment exactly 'Skip tests' on an epic from factory:design-approved onward to close every open case as factory:test-skipped without running it, or on one test(<epic>) case to skip that case alone; bug reports are never skipped. An epic already past G2 when this file lands has no plan; comment 'Plan tests' on it to write one. bug_reports lets a tester raise what no case predicted: commenting 'Bug' on an epic (with the report underneath), or filing an issue labelled factory:bug, opens a bug(<epic>) sub-issue and files an ordinary task to fix it onto the epic branch (§4c). Absent, it follows system_tests; set it false to keep the cases without the bugs, or set it true with system_tests false for exploratory testing with no written plan. simulate (optional, §4b Simulated cases) is for a repo with a simulated environment whose test runner posts a commit status after each staging deploy: {pack: the scenario directory, guide: the repo's guide to what can be simulated and how, status_context: the status the run posts, run_repo: the repo whose Actions run carries the report, report_artifact: its artifact name (default sim-scenarios-report), simulators: {what is simulated: the repo that simulates it}}. With it, the Test Planner marks each case 'Execution: simulated' or 'manual' with the reason, opens one simulated-tests task per epic (a scenario per simulated case, each naming the case in 'covers') and a gap task in a simulator's repo for behaviour no simulator has; after a staging merge the factory reads the run's report and labels each simulated case factory:test-passed or factory:test-failed, opening no fix by itself — comment 'Test Failed' on the case for a fix, or 'Test Failed, expedite' (an expedite approver) for a fix that advances itself. A staging approver comments 'Simulate tests' on an epic planned before the block existed. Without the block nothing here changes.
